svg.title: Hub-and-spoke and Virtual WAN network topologies in an Azure landing zone
svg.desc: Layout follows the two topology diagrams on Microsoft Learn. Top: traditional hub-and-spoke. The Connectivity subscription holds a DDoS Protection plan, Azure DNS with private zones, ExpressRoute circuits, and two hub virtual networks, one for region 1 and one for region N, each with Azure Firewall and VPN or ExpressRoute gateways. The two hubs are joined by global virtual network peering. The workload landing zone subscription holds a spoke virtual network for region 1 and one for region N, each with UDRs and network security groups, and each peered to its hub. Bottom: Azure Virtual WAN. The Connectivity subscription holds the same shared items and one Azure Virtual WAN containing a Virtual WAN hub for region 1 and one for region N, joined by a hub-to-hub connection, each with Azure Firewall and VPN or ExpressRoute gateways. The workload landing zone virtual networks connect to the hubs with Virtual WAN hub connections. Icons are official Azure icons.
svg.text: Traditional hub-and-spoke: you manage routing and security
Azure Virtual WAN: Microsoft manages the hubs

As in Learn's diagrams, the shared items (DDoS Protection plan, Azure DNS, ExpressRoute, firewall, gateways) are in the Connectivity subscription and the workload networks are in landing zone subscriptions.
